label: Late original-phase / <DEL> steps (absolute t >= 4), before copying starts
explanation: Fires only during the input half of the sequence, from absolute step 4 onward, through the <DEL> step. It never fires at t=0-2 and is essentially silent during the copy phase (261 of 2.7M steps). The <DEL> step carries 44% of activation mass (active on 45% of delimiters) and gives the largest activations, with the top examples near 0.9-1.0 of max. Original-phase firing peaks at t=5-6. Activation tends to ramp up over the last few original tokens into <DEL>. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token (91% of mass has in_first=1). The predicate (phase <= 1) & (t >= 4) covers more than 99% of activation mass, but precision is only about 0.32: within that window the feature is off on roughly two-thirds of steps. Whether it fires depends diffusely on sequence content. First tokens x/c/t/e/w and certain previous tokens (l, q, n, y) raise the rate about 2x, but no simple token rule recovers precision; restricting first_tok to a set raised precision to 0.55 but cut recall to 0.45.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: x, c, t, e, w, d; least: j, k, p, b) and the third original token (most: p, r, m, h, x, i; least: n, e, w, c); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
